title: Seller handoff mini-playbook (pilot acceleration) - raw
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, seller-focused handoff playbook intended to accelerate pilot activation for technical buyers (platform teams, integration architects). It is intentionally lightweight so sellers can paste a tailored version into a customer email or SE ticket.

Audience:
Primary: AEs/SEs who need a repeatable checklist to move from qualification -> pilot kickoff.
Secondary: Solutions engineers and platform operation owners who run the first 1-3-week pilot.

When to use:
- Customer shows platform-level interest and asks for a short technical proof-of-concept.
- Org wants predictable time-to-first-meaningful-result (TFR).
- Seller has built initial trust: signed NDA or POC agreement, basic budget cleared.

One-line sell:
“30-day pilot template that proves latency, cost, and fallback economics on Redwood with minimal engineering lift — includes a play-by-play handoff checklist for SEs and SREs.”

Quick seller checklist (pasteable):
- Goal: Define measurable success (throughput, p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, quality checks).
- Target model(s): pick one recommended hostable variant (e.g., rdx-7b-q8, rdx-13b-fp16) and an inexpensive fallback (r-dx-3b-quant).
- Data: sample prompt set + 100 representative user messages (anonymized).
- Traffic shape: expected concurrency and typical request size (tokens).
- Timeline: Kickoff (Day 0), baseline test (Day 2), integrated test (Day 7), pilot review (Day 14).
- Ops contact: attach SE + SRE on the ticket.

30-min technical briefing template (for seller -> SE handoff call):
1) 3-slide opener (2 min): use-case, value metric (e.g., reduce average handle time), and desired outcome of pilot.
2) Architecture sketch (5 min): where Redwood sits (hosted/dedicated/private), network path, data residency needs, keys/KMS.
3) Performance targets (5 min): p95/p99 latency target, tokens/sec, e2e SLO.
4) Failure modes (5 min): acceptable fallback behavior — degrade from rdx-13b -> rdx-3b vs queue-shed.
5) Pilot plan & quick runbook (10 min): who does what D0-D14, test dataset, rollbacks.
6) Q&A & next steps (3 min).

Pilot runbook (ops-friendly, copy to ticket):
- Stage A: Baseline (hosted API)
  - Create API key scoped to pilot.
  - Run 500 synthetic requests (mix sizes). Record p50/p95/p99 latencies and total token cost.
  - Capture sample outputs for quality review.
- Stage B: Integrate path (sandbox integration)
  - Wire prefix caching if app uses repeated prompts. Enable KV caching suggestion from Optimize.
  - Run ramp to expected concurrency (10–30 min soak). Validate tail latency and error rate.
- Stage C: Resilience tests
  - Simulate model fallback: reduce capacity to force routing to fallback model; confirm acceptable output & semantics.
  - Validate canary rollback: deploy older model version and confirm consistent responses.
- Stage D: Review & close
  - Deliver SLO report and cost delta table.
  - Collect qualitative feedback from PM/engineer. Decide next-step (dedicated commit, private evaluation, or iterate).

Pilot success metrics (suggested default):
- Quant: p95 latency < target (seller-specified), error rate < 0.5%, cost per 1k tokens within agreed threshold.
- Qual: 70% of sampled responses meet rubric (precision/recall/style).
- Business: Demonstrated 20% improvement in the chosen value metric (e.g., triage accuracy, time saved).

Common engineering objections + suggested demo responses (short):
- "We need sub-100ms at 256 tokens" -> Ask for typical concurrency and traffic shape. Offer dedicated capacity baseline: show past perf numbers for rdx-7b on A100 with continuous batching and expected p95. If urgent, propose a 48-hr dedicated smoke test.
- "We can’t send PII" -> Offer private deployment option or token-level PII scrub flow. Ask for sample payload to scope KMS/HSM needs.
- "Cost is unpredictable" -> Show Optimize’s batch/caching suggestions and run estimation on pilot dataset (quick calc: avg tokens * projected daily reqs * model rate). Include a worked example in ticket.
- "How do we fail gracefully?" -> Describe routing policies: region fallback, model-size fallback, and automatic queue-shed. Provide sample fallback policy snippet sellers can copy into conversation.

Sample seller script snippets (one-liners to paste in email):
- "We’ll run a focused 14-day pilot with our SE. Expect a baseline report within 3 business days showing latency, token cost, and 10 sample outputs for quality review."
- "If you need data isolation, we can run this pilot in Dedicated or Private and bring up a short-term reserved pool for the test window."

Handoff ticket template (fields to include in Jira/SE ticket):
- Summary: Pilot kickoff: <account> — <use-case short>
- Description: Business goal, expected traffic, sample prompts (attach), security constraints, timeline.
- Acceptance criteria: p95/p99 targets, cost limit, sample quality rubric.
- Contacts: AE, SE, SRE, Customer PM (email + slack).
- Linked artifacts: Confluence playbook, NDA, pilot agreement.

Canary & rollback checklist (quick):
- Pre-canary: snapshot baseline metrics, confirm monitoring hooks and tracing enabled.
- Canary: route 5–10% of traffic to variant for 1-2 hours; watch error rate, p99, and semantic drift (manual spot-check).
- Rollback: automatic if error rate > 1% or p99 increases > 2x. Manual rollback if quality rubric fails on sample set.

Data & privacy caveats:
- If customer requires no raw data leave-hosted, propose: 1) on-prem/private deploy; or 2) host with token scrub + short retention + KMS.
- Always capture data-handling requirement in ticket and log to compliance.

Elevator metrics cheat-sheet (pasteable to customer):
- Typical hosted pilot: 2–14 days, 3–5% of production traffic, p95 latency 120–600ms depending on model/seq length, iterative cost estimate provided after baseline test.

Open questions / things to validate before finalizing pilot:
- Does account require SOC2 + FedRAMP coverage? If yes, route to enterprise sales motion.
- Which cloud region(s) do they need? (NA/EU/APAC)
- Any regulatory constraints preventing use of hosted endpoints?

Next steps (immediate):
- AE: confirm pilot scope and send NDA/pilot agreement.
- SE: schedule 30-min kick with customer and SRE within 48 hrs.
- SRE: prepare ephemeral pool (if requested) and enable monitoring hook.

Notes to self (fragmented, because this is a working doc):
- Add a short worked example: sample tokens * daily calls -> monthly cost estimate.
- Build a one-click email template in Notion for sellers.
- Need a short internal video (3–4m) showing how to force fallback and interpret SLO logs.
- Check with Platform eng on more recent p95 numbers for rdx-13b on T4 vs A100.

References / quick links to copy into ticket:
- Pilot playbook (confluence): confluence://INF/playbooks/pilot-accelerator
- SE kickoff template (github): github://redwood-inference/pilot-templates/README.md
- SLA & security note: confluence://INF/security/sla-note

End of doc — this is a living sketch. Copy/trim as needed for customer communication.
